title: Development of a non-interventional, multicenter registry for immune-mediated neuropathies with a study-specific biobank (Immunemediated Neuropathies Biomaterial and Data Register - INHIBIT-Register)
summary:
Autoimmune neuropathies (AIN) are a large group within immune-mediated diseases of the peripheral nerves. The detection of AIN among the various neuropathies plays an important role as they require targeted treatment. With 2.2-10.2 patients per 100,000 inhabitants, this heterogeneous group of diseases is a rare but probably underdiagnosed disease. So far, it has not yet been possible to define a targeted therapy for the various subtypes and course forms. In order to remedy this supply deficit, a structural and translational recording of the disease progression and patient characteristics is essential.
The aim of this project is to establish a longitudinal cohort with previously and newly diagnosed AIN patients as well as all patients with immune-mediated neuropathies. Focus is on autoimmune-mediated neuropathies in order to better characterize the broad spectrum of this disease. In addition to a very detailed clinical and technical characterization (anamnesis, medical history, structured scoring of symptoms and quality of life, therapy data, additional technical examinations), the systematic collection and storage of biosamples in a study-specific biobank are also required. This study-specific biobank will, for example, store blood samples and urine samples, cerebrospinal fluid, skin and nerve biopsies, which are obtained during the routine diagnosis of the disease. For this purpose, the IMMUNMEDIATED NEUROPATHIES BIOMATERIAL AND DATA REGISTERS - called INHIBIT register - with a project-specific central biobank will be founded at the UK RUB - Clinic for Neurology at St. Josef Hospital Bochum. The INHIBT Register is a voluntary association of scientists from cooperating clinics and centers that specialize in immune-mediated neuropathies. INHIBIT offers the cooperating clinics a common structure and organization for research into immune-mediated neuropathies.

interventions.name: All participating patients are examined at baseline, after 6 months, then annually, and biomaterial samples are stored. If necessary, interim visits can be added for the same purpose.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a suspected or confirmed diagnosis of immune neuropathy are included. These include all autoimmune neuropathies (acute inflammatory polyneuropathy = GBS; chronic inflammatory neuropathies = CIN / type of CIDP), as well as all paraneoplastic neuropathies, vasculitic neuropathies, paraproteinemic neuropathies and pathogen-mediated neuropathies as well as accompanying neuropathies in systemic neuropathies. Diabetic polyneuropathy is a special form of immune neuropathy and is also part of the study group. The exact mechanism of critical illness polyneuropathy has not yet been clarified, but there are indications of an immunological cause, so that these patients are also included.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who
• do not give consent to participate in the study
• are unable to provide information themselves or through an authorized representative or have serious psychiatric illnesses
• In the case of contraindications for individual follow-up examinations such as neurography, QST, corneal microscopy or skin biopsy, the respective examination will not be performed.
